name: Bermersheim vor der Hoehe
summary: A village in Rhenish Hesse, by long tradition the birthplace of Hildegard of Bingen about 1098, and the point from which she was given to the church as a child.
overview: Bermersheim vor der Höhe is a small village in the Alzey-Worms country of the Rhineland, in the archdiocese of Mainz.
It is identified as the birthplace of Hildegard of Bingen, born there about 1098 to a family of the lower nobility, and has no separate medieval significance.
knownFor: Traditional birthplace of Hildegard of Bingen, about 1098

imageInfo.note: A modern administrative map, used because the village preserves no medieval structure connected with Hildegard and none is photographed on Commons. It shows the modern district boundaries rather than any medieval jurisdiction: in Hildegard's lifetime the place lay in Rhenish Franconia within the archdiocese of Mainz.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Bermersheim vor der Höhe lies in Rhenish Hesse, the rolling farm country south-west of Mainz, and is distinguished by name from the other Bermersheim near Worms. It is a village of a few hundred people and was not much larger in the twelfth century.

Its entire claim on history is one birth. Hildegard of Bingen — abbess, visionary, composer, medical writer and correspondent of popes and emperors — was born there about 1098, and the identification is consistent in the tradition even though no contemporary document states it outright.

contentSections.title: The family
paragraphs: Hildegard's parents were Hildebert of Bermersheim and Mechthild, members of the lower nobility who held their position in the service of the counts of Sponheim. That connection matters more than the village itself: it explains how a child from a minor Rhenish family came to be placed with Jutta of Sponheim, the count's daughter.

She is described in her Vita as the tenth child, which her biographers connected to the idea of a tithe owed to God, though only seven older siblings can actually be documented. Two of her brothers became clerics and a sister entered religion, which was an ordinary pattern for a family of that rank with more children than land.

contentSections.title: From Bermersheim to Disibodenberg
paragraphs: Hildegard was given to the church as a child oblate and enclosed with Jutta of Sponheim in an anchorage attached to the Benedictine monastery of Disibodenberg, on All Saints' Day, 1 November 1112. The Vita says she was eight when she was professed; the evidence of the enclosure date suggests she was about fourteen, and the discrepancy is one of the genuine difficulties in her biography rather than a detail to smooth over.

The anchorage grew into a women's community, and when Jutta died in 1136 Hildegard was elected magistra. About 1150 she moved her nuns to a new foundation at Rupertsberg near Bingen, over the objections of the monks of Disibodenberg, and founded a second house at Eibingen in 1165. She died in 1179.

contentSections.title: The village and the saint
paragraphs: Bermersheim has no castle, no abbey and no medieval church of note, and it did not benefit from Hildegard's fame in the way a shrine town would — her cult was attached to Rupertsberg, Eibingen and Bingen, where her relics are, not to the place of her birth.

The village commemorates the connection in its parish dedication and in modern markers, and it appears in the archive for the same reason many birthplaces do: because a biography has to begin somewhere, and being specific about where is better than leaving a life to start in mid-air. It is honestly a small place with one large association.

timeline.title: Birth of Hildegard
timeline.description: Hildegard is born at Bermersheim to Hildebert and Mechthild, of the lower Rhenish nobility.

timeline.title: Enclosed at Disibodenberg
timeline.description: She is enclosed with Jutta of Sponheim in the anchorage attached to the Benedictine monastery.

timeline.title: Elected magistra
timeline.description: On Jutta's death the community elects Hildegard to lead it.

timeline.title: The move to Rupertsberg
timeline.description: She takes her nuns to a new house near Bingen despite opposition from the monks of Disibodenberg.

timeline.title: Eibingen founded
timeline.description: A second community is established across the Rhine.

timeline.title: Death at Rupertsberg
timeline.description: Hildegard dies in the monastery she founded, eighty-one years after leaving Bermersheim as a child.
